creative_brief.emotional_promise: Turn thirty small printed parts into a formidable mountain locomotive whose lineage, assembly, and gentle hand-guided motion are immediately legible.
creative_brief.format_rationale: A compact landscape sequence keeps each task to one spread-sized page, leaves the exact locomotive imagery wide enough to read, and can remain in the model box as a durable build and care reference.
teaching_arc: Recognize the finished Ouray No. 100 and its intended desk-scale character
Account for all 16 locomotive and 14 tender-and-coupling parts
Seat and retain the locomotive wheelsets before adding landmark fittings
Build two free-yawing tender trucks and orient the coupling bars
Connect, guide, yaw, and release the two bodies without forcing them
Diagnose binding wheels, stiff trucks, and a missed coupling
Store, clean, and handle the model safely while retaining its historical limits
typography: Display and navigation — embedded Vera Bold
creative_brief.visual_motif: Deep railroad green fields, brass route markers, oxblood cautions, and cream drafting-card panels evoke a restrained nineteenth-century shop folio without imitating a museum document.

findings: Page 5 cropped the third signature state, preventing the connect-roll-release sequence from being read visually.
Page 6 buried the fact that fit and rolling were assessed digitally only.
Pages 3–6 mentioned adhesive without giving maker-guidance safety direction.
resolved_changes: Reframed the exact signature source to show all three complete states aligned over their numbered action cards.
Promoted the physical-print limitation to a high-contrast DIGITAL-ONLY CHECK callout.
Added adhesive ventilation, contact, age, and supervision guidance and wrapped the small-parts warning inside its panel.
